construct: 5 sibling options where ONE is SELECTED - a distinct fill (rgb(219, 234, 254)) and weight among four identical siblings
why: The selected option is the repetition problem wearing its most consequential face: five near-identical children where the one that DIFFERS is the only one carrying the component's actual value. Five siblings is above the inverse rule's >=3 threshold, so a repetition collapse is eligible here; if it happens, the list still looks like a list and the selection is simply gone.

canvas.note: the selected option is a frame with its own fill among four unfilled siblings

mustHave: the listbox shows exactly 5 options, stacked vertically
exactly ONE option (the 3rd, 'Gamma') carries a tinted fill
the selected option's text is bolder than the other four
the other 4 options have no fill of their own
